title: Embedding/Reranker Regression Pipeline: drift alerts, offline recall/precision evals, and config gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated regression pipeline that ties changes in embedding model variants and reranker configs to offline quality metrics (recall, precision, MRR) and drift signals, and gates deploys when regressions exceed thresholds.

Scope: offline batch eval harness + nightly drift scoring + signal aggregator + alerting + a config gating checklist for Dedicated/Private deploys. Must support multiple embedding dimensions and reranker scoring variants, be reproducible, and integrate with existing Console dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
- A reproducible offline eval job that computes recall@k, precision@k, and normalized MRR for the canonical dataset and can be run per model + config.
- Nightly drift job that computes embedding distribution drift (cosine mean shift, covariance trace) and reranker score distribution shift; stores results in time series DB.
- Aggregator that combines quality delta and drift signals into a single regression score and evaluates against threshold rules (actions: warn, block, require review).
- Alerting configured in PagerDuty for block-level regressions and Slack notifications for warnings; alerts link to a PR summary and evaluation artifact.
- Gating policy documented in Console rollouts: small delta (<1% recall drop) auto-allow, medium delta (1-3%) require PM + SE review, large delta (>3%) block.
- End-to-end demo run and dashboard story for PM/SE review.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Use existing canonical evaluation set (30k labeled pairs) rather than synthetic augmentation to reduce false positives from noisy labels. Trade-off: smaller coverage of tail cases.
- For drift, compute both embedding-level statistics and reranker-score distribution changes. Use KS test + shifted cosine mean; KS is sensitive but can be noisy for small samples. We will smooth with a rolling 7-day baseline.
- Aggregation rule is intentionally conservative to avoid blocking too many rollouts: if recall drops >2% OR drift score > 0.12 AND reranker MRR drops >1% then block. These numbers are provisional pending calibration during first two cycles.
- Performance: offline eval should complete within the nightly window (<3 hours). If longer, we will shard the batch by query buckets.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Embedding+Reranker+Regression+Design
- GitHub eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-harness/pull/402 (draft)
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embedding-reranker-regressions
- Example PR template that triggers eval run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/.github/blob/main/pull_request_template.md

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype: run offline eval nightly for staging models for two weeks (no gating, collect signals).
2) Calibration: tune thresholds with PM/Applied ML using collected history.
3) Soft block: enforce gating for non-critical releases (require manual review).
4) Full block: enforce gating for production model swaps.

Notes for Dedicated/Private: gating will be advisory for on-prem until customer opt-in due to different upgrade cadences and PR implications.
